headline: AMD chief Lisa Su held more than three hours of talks with Samsung's chip head in Seoul as AMD seeks more memory and Samsung wants chip-making orders.
score_reason: Lowered 1 from 6: the meeting took place on 7 Oct, before the window, and Su gave no sign of a deal.
importance_line: A foundry order from AMD would help Samsung's contract chip-making business and a steadier memory supply would help AMD's AI chips, but Su gave no details and the memory-for-foundry link is the industry's interpretation.
summary: Chosun Biz reports that AMD chief executive Lisa Su met Samsung Electronics' chip division head Jun Young-hyun in Seoul on 7 Oct 2026 for over three hours, calling it "a very good discussion" but giving no details on progress toward AMD using Samsung's contract chip-making (foundry) business. The paper says the industry reads the meeting as bridging AMD's need for more high-bandwidth memory and Samsung's wish for foundry orders; the two firms signed a memorandum of understanding in March covering HBM4 and DDR5 memory supply and talks on foundry production.
notes: TechPowerUp page (consent wall) unreadable; story read at Chosun Biz (own reporting) and corroborated by Business Korea (also reports Su met SK hynix's Kwak Noh-jung the same day). The 'memory for foundry orders' framing in TechPowerUp's headline is an industry interpretation, so stated as such.
